request.spec:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people list can be sorted on the screen: a select of added, name, grade or due-total, per
user's screen. Sorting by name compares as names are compared; by due-total puts n/a last; equal
keys keep list order. Sorting changes only what the screen shows: the positions, the rollup lines
and every action in list order are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people list now has a sort select (`sort-by`), and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

All the changes are in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`:

- **The select:** it offers added, name, grade and due-total, and sits next to "Show retired".
- **Per user's screen:** each browser keeps its own choice. It starts at "added" and stays in place when the sheet is reloaded. Nothing goes to the server or the audit file, so another user still sees the list in added order.
- **Sorting:**
  - **name** compares names the way the app already does elsewhere, ignoring case and outer spaces, so "ada" comes before "Ben".
  - **grade** uses the grade in force on the sheet's today.
  - **due-total** uses the capped due-total, lowest first, with n/a last.
  - People with equal keys keep their list order.
- **What it doesn't touch:** only the displayed rows are reordered. The stored positions, move up/down, the rollup lines, the exports and the bulk actions all still use the list order.
